ConsoleOffer.description: What a status says of a machine's graphical console: its protocol, or `none` and why.

note.description: Why there is none, or what it needs (an extension pack).

unavailable.description:
Why it can't be shown now, as the status found it on a running machine: its hypervisor
gives it no display (a VM started without one). None when it can, or wasn't looked at: the
machine doesn't run, it has none, or it is reached through Proxmox's API, which a status
doesn't open.

ConsoleProtocol.description: The protocol a graphical console speaks.

oneOf.description: VNC (RFB).
RDP (VirtualBox's remote display).
None the runner reaches.

Desired.description: What a user wants of a run: set by the commands, never by an observation.

oneOf.description: Up and ready.
Parked: stopped, what it created kept.
Nothing of it left.

ErrorCode.description: The stable code of a failure, the same in the Rust API and the event stream (`error.code`).

oneOf.description:
The folder isn't a project Isothrum runs: it holds no Compose file, Vagrantfile or
Terraform module, or the files of several formats with none named.

The manifest needs something this runner doesn't do (a target that doesn't run on this
host, a delivery its driver doesn't take, an action of another driver's, a step with no
command for this host), or the call asks the run for something its target can't do (a
console into a Compose service with no VM, a Vagrant VM joined to another network).
A file or folder couldn't be read or written, or a socket on this computer bound.
Another process runs an operation on this run, or holds the home's slot pick.
A tool a step runs isn't installed.
A step's tool ran and failed.

A tool the run needs is installed, but its probe got no answer from it (Docker's engine
stopped, or not this account's to reach): the message says what the tool said.
A tool answers at a version older than the run needs.

A step showed no progress for its time limit, or ran to the ceiling every step stops at,
and was stopped, with what it started (the `error` event's `detail` says which).

A download (what a step needs, fetched in a phase of its own before it: a Compose start's
images, a Vagrant start's boxes; or a step the manifest marks a download) showed no
progress for as long as a download may, and was stopped.

A download couldn't be made: its tool failed (the message says why: a registry or a box
catalog refusing it, a name it doesn't know, the network). A failure for the network that
passes (a connection reset, refused or timed out, a gateway's 502, 503 or 504) was tried
again first, up to three more times: the message is the last try's.
The run is already up.
The run is recorded on another place (server or account) than the one asked for.
A host port the run publishes is taken.
The manifest has no park steps for that mode.
Nothing of the run, or not every one of its machines, is left to resume.
The run isn't up.
A ready condition didn't hold.
A required secret or input has no value.

A value or secret that can't be handed to the tools (its name empty or holding `=`, a
NUL in it).
A run name that can't name a run.

The run's Vagrant provider is missing, unknown, not on this host, refused by the run, or
lacks its plugin.

The elevation Hyper-V's commands need couldn't be had or was lost: the permission prompt
declined or unanswered, the elevated session not started or ended before the operation
(the message says which).
A machine the run doesn't have.
The run has several machines the call could mean, and it named none.
A network the run doesn't have.
A deployment can't be taken over as a run.

The operation was cut short before it ended (its future dropped: an embedder's cancel, the
command line's Ctrl-C or SIGTERM); the tools it started were asked to stop, and are ended
once they have, or 30 seconds later.

The embedder was asked for something that makes no sense (the command line: a run folder
with no manifest, a value missing or malformed), so no operation started.

The machine has no graphical console to reach: its target or provider gives none (the
error says why), it isn't running, or its hypervisor doesn't say where it is.

The server the run is on (Proxmox VE, ESXi) refused the run's credentials: its API
answered 401 or 403, or its tool said the sign-in failed (an API token revoked, a password
changed).

A file of the runner's own (a record, a ledger entry) is there but isn't what it wrote:
not JSON, or another version's shape.

The run's state machine has no such move (a park of a parked run, a resume of a ready
one), or a resource row can't move that way.
The run moved between the read and the write that would have moved it: try again.
The home's store was written by a newer runner.
The home's store isn't a database this runner reads, or holds what it doesn't write.
A live process holds the lease asked for.

MachineState.description: A machine's state, as its engine reports it.

oneOf.description: Running.
Running, but failing its health check.
Exited with this code (a job that finished, or a machine that died).
Created or stopped, not running.
Not there.
Something else, as the engine says it.

Not read: another process acts on it (Vagrant's lock on the machine, held by a `vagrant
up` that isn't this runner's), so its state is whatever that action leaves.

MachineStatus.description: One machine of the run, as its tool reports it.

address.description:
The address it is reached at itself, when its tool says one another computer reaches (a
VM on a bridged or host-only network, a server's VM, a cloud instance); none for one
reached only through its published ports. On ESXi, which forwards no port to this
computer, a machine's ports answer at this address.

console.description:
Its graphical console, as its hypervisor offers it; none for a machine with no screen to
speak of (a container), and while not [`Status::live`].

name.description: Its name in the project (a Compose service, a Vagrant machine, a module's VM).

NativeApp.description:
The hypervisor's own app that shows a running VM's screen in a window of its own, and what of
it this computer must have (any one of `needs`).

name.description: Its name as its maker writes it (`VirtualBox`, `VMware Fusion`): what a button names.

needs.description:
What opens it, best first: the program or app [`NativeConsole::ways`] runs, in the same
order.

NativeNeed.description: What of a hypervisor's app must be on this computer for a way to open it.

oneOf.description: A program, by its name on `PATH` or its full path.
A macOS app bundle.
The default browser (a web console).

OutputValue.description:
An output's value (a Terraform module's output). A sensitive one shows as `***` wherever it
is written out (its JSON, its `Debug`, an event); the runner keeps the value itself for the
embedder ([`OutputValue::revealed`]).

value.description: Its value, when it can be read; `***` when it is sensitive.

oneOf.description: TCP.
UDP.

Provider.description:
A Vagrant provider: the hypervisor `vagrant up --provider` takes. Exhaustive: whoever detects
or offers providers (`isothrum-machine`) fails to compile until a new one has its row.

oneOf.description: VirtualBox.
VMware Workstation or Fusion.
Hyper-V.
Parallels Desktop.
libvirt (KVM).
QEMU.
UTM.
An ESXi server.

PublishedPort.description: A published port: where a machine's port answers on the host.

host_port.description: The host port it is reached at, at the machine's host address.

protocol.description: `tcp` or `udp`; `None` when the tool doesn't say (Vagrant's `port`), never guessed.

oneOf.description: Being created by an `up`.
Up, every member machine running.
Something of it exists, but not every member machine runs (a failed start, a machine down).
Being parked.
Parked: stopped, what it created kept.
Being resumed.
Being brought up to date with its manifest by an `update`.
Being removed by a `down`.
Nothing of it exists.

desired.description:
What the user wants of the run (the last operation that set it: `up`, `park`, `down`);
none for a run never recorded. With `state`, whether the run is where it should be.

failed_cause.description: Why the run failed, when its recorded state is `failed`.

live.description:
Whether the machines and outputs were read from the engine now. False while an operation
holds the run (in this process or another), whose tools a read would contend with (Vagrant
refuses to read a VM's state while a `vagrant up` provisions it): they are then as the
runner last read them (none before it ever did), and the outputs the engine itself gives
are left out.

native.description:
The hypervisor's own app the run's VMs open in ([`crate::Running::native_console`]); none
where there is none (containers, QEMU), and while not [`Status::live`].

outputs.description:
What the project gives back (a module's outputs), as read; none while not
[`Status::live`].

provider.description: The Vagrant provider it uses, when it has one.

state.description:
Where it stands. While an operation holds the run: the moving state it is in (`creating`
through an `up`), else, before it records one or for an operation that leaves the run as
it was meanwhile (an `update`: `ready`), the state the run's record holds.
